# Car size and model attributes {#sec-dd-racf}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$racf
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
```

## Overview

These columns attach to each car the size, mass and official emissions of its
model, from the RACF car fleet. That fleet is DfT's car fleet by make, model,
year of first use and fuel, enriched with each model's SMMT segment
(supermini, SUV and so on; @sec-vehicle-types) and with its mass, dimensions,
CO~2~, energy use and electric range from the EU type-approval and Dutch RDW
registers. It holds counts and model attributes only, not vehicle records.

- **`racf_link_level`** says how the car was linked to the RACF fleet:
  - `model`: the same make, DfT generic model and model string, year of first
    use and fuel group;
  - `genmodel`: failing that, the same make, generic model, year and fuel
    group, averaging over the generic model's model strings;
  - `none`: not linked.

  Only cars (`body_type` Cars) are linked, so the column and every `racf_`
  column is blank for other vehicles.
- **`racf_smmt_type`** is the SMMT segment with the largest fleet among the
  linked RACF rows, and **`racf_suv_share`** the share of that fleet the SMMT
  calls a crossover / SUV or an off-roader.
- **The size and mass columns** are the EU mass in running order
  (`racf_mass_kg`), the RDW kerb weight, length, width and height, the
  wheelbase, and the footprint (wheelbase times track, in m²).
- **The emissions and energy columns** are the EU NEDC and WLTP CO~2~ figures
  in g/km, the energy use in Wh/km and the electric range in km.
- **`racf_eu_exact_share`** is the share of the linked RACF fleet matched to
  the EU type-approval data for its exact year. The rest borrows another
  year's or fuel's values.

Each value is the fleet-weighted mean over the linked RACF rows with a
plausible value, so it describes the model, not the individual car. How the
link is made is set out in the methodology,
[section 6](../../reports/methodology.md#stage-4-derived-fields-and-number-plates)
and [section 9.3](../../reports/methodology.md#the-racf-smmt-linked-fleet).

::: {.callout-important title="Model values, not measurements"}
A car's `racf_co2_nedc` is the average for its model, year and fuel, not its
own figure, which is in `co2` (@sec-dd-emissions). The `racf_` columns are
best used to describe groups of cars, such as the fleet's average size or the
share of SUVs, and for cars with `racf_eu_exact_share` well below 1 they are
borrowed from another year or fuel.
:::

`racf_link_level`, `racf_suv_share` and `racf_eu_exact_share` are in the
maximal table only. The SMMT segment and the size, mass, CO~2~ and energy
columns are also in the simplified table.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-racf
#| tbl-cap: "Car size and model attribute columns."
dict_table("racf")
```

## Coverage

`racf_link_level` is present for the `r cov_pct(cs, "racf_link_level")` of
vehicles that are cars. Most of those link to a model, so
`racf_smmt_type` is present for `r cov_pct(cs, "racf_smmt_type")` of all
vehicles. The other columns are present only where the linked RACF rows have
a plausible value, and their coverage follows the registers they come from
(@fig-dd-racf):

- **The EU mass and footprint** and the **RDW kerb weight** are present for
  most cars: `racf_mass_kg` for `r cov_pct(cs, "racf_mass_kg")` of all
  vehicles. The RDW width and length are present for fewer.
- **NEDC CO~2~** applies to cars approved before the WLTP test replaced it,
  so `racf_co2_nedc` is present for most cars first used up to 2020 and
  `racf_co2_wltp` for most of those first used from 2018
  (`r cov_year("racf_co2_wltp", 2022)` of vehicles first used in 2022). Cars
  first used from 2018 to 2020 often have both.
- **Energy use and electric range** apply only to plug-in cars, so they are
  present for `r cov_pct(cs, "racf_e_range_km", digits = 1)` of vehicles,
  rising for the newest.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-racf-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-racf
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value in selected RACF columns, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 4.6
coverage_plot(c("racf_link_level", "racf_mass_kg", "racf_co2_nedc",
                "racf_co2_wltp"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("racf"))
```
